shipped_default_operating_point.name: balanced_top5
shipped_default_operating_point.selection_rule: Pre-hoc, named rule: first operating point, in the fixed candidate order active_top10 -> balanced_top5 -> selective_top2 -> sniper_top1, satisfying ALL of (a) n > 100, (b) positive avg net return/trade, (c) Wilson-95% lower bound within reach of 50%.
shipped_default_operating_point.why_balanced_top5: n=111 (>100); avg net return/trade +0.17% (positive); Wilson95=[45.7%, 63.9%] (lower bound close to 50%). First candidate to clear all three conditions.
shipped_default_operating_point.why_not_active_top10: n=320 clears the sample-size bar but avg net return/trade is -0.05% -- fails the positive-expectancy condition. This is also the only point at which the model currently trades at full frequency (see hunt_config.json runtime_gating_note).
shipped_default_operating_point.why_not_selective_top2_or_sniper_top1: n=34 and n=11 respectively -- both fail n>100 regardless of their higher (but far noisier, per their wide Wilson intervals) win rates and profit factors.
shipped_default_operating_point.fixes_prior_process: MODEL.md previously narrated the 'balanced' point as though chosen by eyeballing holdout profit factor across all four candidates -- a mild form of holdout-peeking on WHICH threshold to ship. The threshold VALUES themselves were and remain leak-free (quantile_source=train_oof_pooled, train-only OOF quantiles). This field replaces that post-hoc narrative with an explicit, falsifiable, pre-hoc rule; applying the rule resolves to the same point (balanced_top5).
